factor_diagnostics.value_notes: NOAA/NEFSC trawl-survey summaries report seasonal adult bottom-water occurrence: roughly 3–21 °C in spring (most 9–12 °C) and 8–28 °C in fall (most 16–27 °C). A warming study reports seasonal exposure around 6–27 °C. These are seasonal bottom-water and northern-stock observations, not a universal surface-temperature preference curve. Florida Museum describes the species as mainly north of northeastern Florida, with extreme South Florida records during cold winters. The configured 15–24 °C SST band and 18–22 °C ideal are not locally calibrated.
